extracted.intended_audience: pianists, piano students and teachers (classical performance/interpretation)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and interpretive guidance for classical pianists and teachers covering touch, tone production, phrasing, practice methods, memorization, and stylistic/edition fidelity. Emphasizes concrete technical principles and how to apply them in practice and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point_of_contact and finger_action (Rubinstein principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keys are not to be struck with high finger action, nor is the direct end of the finger used; the point of contact is rather just back of the tip, between that and the ball of the finger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a half staccato touch rather than plain legato for clarity in rapid passages: 'The tones, when separated a hair's breadth from each other, take on a lighter, more vibrant, radiant quality; they are really like strings of pearls.' Avoid high, tension-producing finger action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure_touch / expressive_caressing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pressure touch—pressing and caressing the keys—feeling for the quality wanted; mentally hear the tone and produce it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think the tone before producing it: 'I think it, I hear it mentally, and I can make it.' Use tactile pressure to shape sound rather than only mechanical key-strokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight_touch and whole-body engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Weight touch is a necessity; employ not only arms and shoulders but the whole body to feel and vibrate with the tones of the piano.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow the body to resonate with tone production; develop a weight-led approach rather than purely finger-only motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant_search_for_quality_of_tone
rubrics_metrics.description: A constant search for quality of tone; with right touch and attention one can make any piano give out a beautiful tone, even a poor instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment and listen; refine tone through memory and experience; tone production is individualized and requires ongoing exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorizing_by_concentration_and_mental_work
rubrics_metrics.description: Memorizing comes from deep concentration and intent listening; after sufficient study the music becomes 'a permanent possession.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do substantial mental work away from the instrument: think pieces through, listen mentally, and maintain absolute concentration during performance. Some players advise hand‑separate measures, but the author favors internalization over rote drills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know_orchestral_parts_when_playing_concertos
rubrics_metrics.description: When playing a concerto with orchestra one should know not only the piano part but also each note that the other instruments play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listen intently to both piano and orchestra in performance; mental preparation should include awareness of the full score to avoid being 'lost' if distracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_abstract_technic_practice; derive_exercises_from_music
rubrics_metrics.description: Practising technic for itself alone is not necessary once the principles are mastered; instead make technical exercises out of difficult passages in pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take knotty sections and develop many specific exercises (sometimes 40–50 variations) to address them; this is preferred to generic mechanistic drilling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice_time_and_balance_for_recital_preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: An hour's actual playing each day is sufficient to prepare for a recital (with additional mental study), but serious study may amount to six hours a day overall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between 'actual playing' and other study (mental work, analysis). When preparing new programs, increase total study time; use intense concentrated sessions for difficult pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invent_your_own_technical_exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should discover and invent the technical exercises most beneficial to their own hands rather than depending solely on method books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method books often reflect the hand of their author; tailoring or creating exercises increases effectiveness and enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full_round_exact_tone and distinct_phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Two of the most important principles: full, round, exact tone; and distinct phrasing. Clearness in piano playing is absolutely essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid indistinctness such as slurring over or leaving out notes; enunciate clearly as a vocalist/actor would. Treat every line as something to be articulated and understood by the listener.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arms_and_wrists_relaxed; nail_joint_firm; comfortable_hand_position
rubrics_metrics.description: Arms and wrists must be relaxed. Fingers must often be loose also, but not at the nail joint; that must always be firm. Adopt the hand position most comfortable and convenient, avoiding stiffness or cramping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either high or low wrist is permitted so long as the tone is good; take care that powerful chords do not crush the nail joint—especially important for players with weak hands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use_metronome_in_scales_and_arpeggios; make_exercises_musical
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be scale and arpeggio study, in which the metronome can be used. Strive to make even technical exercises of musical value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Play scales and studies with beautiful quality and variety of tone; treat etudes (e.g., Czerny, Chopin) with the care of a sonata rather than a mechanical drill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity_over_speed (velocity principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid rushing; there is a tendency to play everything too fast. When tone and phrasing are clear, the music will not sound as fast as it actually is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on balance and intelligibility rather than sheer tempo. Use demonstration and comparison to show students how clarity affects perceived tempo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power_from_relaxation_and_trained_fingers
rubrics_metrics.description: Power does not depend on hand size; it is a nervous force that demands relaxed arms and wrists and fingers trained to withstand the weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train fingers to 'stand up' under weight; constantly watch the nail joint firmness; avoid tension while producing power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorization_via_writing_out_the_music
rubrics_metrics.description: A sure way to learn difficult compositions is to write them out from memory—visual memory strengthens retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing a score from memory (or a piano solo) gives vivid impressions; earlier-learned works are more enduring than later ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play_correctly_before_playing_beautifully; healthy_touch
rubrics_metrics.description: To play correctly is of first importance; to play beautifully is the second requirement. A healthy touch is the main thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid playing on the sides of the finger or with sideways stroke as these produce weak, uncertain touch. Emphasize technical correctness as foundation for beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self_criticism_and_analysis_of_every_measure
rubrics_metrics.description: You are always your first hearer; being one's own critic is most difficult. Every line and measure must be analyzed for touch, tone, content and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate critical listening to identify and fix faults; analyze small units (themes, measures) for complete clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make_new_themes_plastic_and_plain
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new theme enters you must make it plain to the listener; all features of the new theme must be plastically brought out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat thematic entries as fresh, audible events—shape them so the listener immediately recognizes and follows them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brilliancy_is_clarity_not_velocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Brilliancy does not depend on velocity but on clarity; what is not clear cannot scintillate nor sparkle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use strongest fingers in brilliant passages, omit the fourth finger when possible; scales intended to be brilliant must not be too rapid, each note round and full, played mezzo-legato so hands together can sound like octaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice_dissonances_until_they_please_the_ear; imitate_orchestral_colors
rubrics_metrics.description: A seemingly discordant passage can be made to sound well by ingeniously seeking out the best in it and practising dissonant chords until they please the ear. Think of orchestral instruments and their different qualities of tone and try to imitate them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color and shade each octave differently; 'coloriren'—seek timbral variety and sympathetic voicing to make harsh intervals agreeable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical_dynamics_training ('practise_soft_as_forte')
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Everything which is to be played softly should be practised forte.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exaggerated practice dynamics to control and secure soft playing in performance; practice contrasts to ensure security of pianissimo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness_and_fidelity_to_score; add_marks_to_elucidate_only
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearness of touch, exactness in phrasing and fingering; the delivery of the composer's idea must be just as indicated—no liberties with the text were permitted. Add marks of phrasing or expression only to elucidate the composer's intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insist on precision and respect for the score; editing or alterations are a sin unless they clarify the composer's meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Piece-specific_technical_and_timbre_adaptations
rubrics_metrics.description: Different works and passages demand specific technical adjustments (e.g., practice octaves with light flexible wrist; for Chopin etude in sixths: 'wrist held rather low, knuckles somewhat high, and the fingers straightened'; elevate wrist for black keys and depress for white keys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt hand posture, wrist level and attack depending on the text: use pivots, raising outer hand-side for extended chords, thumb creep techniques, etc., as required by the piece's character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agitation_and_dynamic_shaping_must_be_thought_out
rubrics_metrics.description: Agitation in playing must not be blind but 'seeing'—dynamics should be planned (e.g., divide a diminuendo of several measures into stations: F, MF, M, P, PP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mapped dynamic stations and planned contrast (pause for contrast, segment climaxes) rather than uncontrolled emotional outbursts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice_octaves_and_specific_etudes_with_targeted_methods
rubrics_metrics.description: For octave technique use light flexible wrist (Kullak Octave School recommended); study certain etudes (Rubinstein, Chopin) for musical and technical value rather than only mechanical drills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select pedagogical literature that addresses the musical and technical demand; apply targeted technical schools (Kullak, Rubinstein) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early_learning_is_enduring; unlearning_difficult
rubrics_metrics.description: Compositions learned in early days are never forgotten; unlearning gives more trouble than learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize correct habits and musical understanding from the start because correcting ingrained faults is harder than learning correctly initially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory_expectations_for_professional_pianists
rubrics_metrics.description: No pianist could be considered an artist unless he or she could play at least two hundred pieces by heart (Von Buelow's opinion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate extensive repertoire memory as a professional standard; the master exemplified enormous memorization ability (including orchestral scores).

rubrics_metrics.name: Slow_gentle_motions_and_spiritualization_of_tone (Sherwood)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use slow, gentle motions in practice and playing; spiritualize the tones, getting behind the notes to find the composer's meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a poetic conception of playing from the first lessons: prioritize tone study and interpretive depth alongside technical development.
